title: Oath Under the Moon
next_chapter_hook: Just as Chen Ji thought the night had ended, Mr. Mo's voice rang out again in his Mental Sea, carrying a solemnity never before heard: 'Chen Ji, the words your father left behind back then... he foresaw this day long ago.'

text.content: Deep night at the Tianqing Sect Arena,一片寂静。 The bustling Arena Platform of the day lay especially solemn beneath the moonlight, the broken Formation Rune Patterns gleaming with faint light, as if still savoring the fierce battles of daylight. Chen Ji stood alone beneath the Courtyard Ancient Pine, his robes gently stirred by the night wind. Mr. Mo's words still echoed in his Mental Sea—that person who had never appeared in his memories actually shared such a profound bond with his father—why had Mr. Mo waited until today to speak of it? He gazed up at the night sky, rare perplexity flickering between his brows. His father had left when he was still young, memories long faded, yet now he was told his father was such a figure... Footsteps suddenly broke his reverie. Chen Ji's eyes narrowed slightly as he quickly gathered his thoughts, his expression resuming that cowardly, mediocre mask. The approaching figure, dressed in Light Garment like moonlight, was Su Qingyao, Inner Disciple Senior Fellow.

dialogue.content: 'You're still not resting at this late hour?' Su Qingyao's voice was as cold and clear as always, but Chen Ji keenly detected an indescribable weariness beneath her tone. Though she maintained the dignity of Inner Disciple Senior Fellow, the exhaustion deep in her eyes was undeniable. Chen Ji slightly bowed, keeping his voice very low: 'Reporting to Senior Sister, the junior couldn't sleep, so I came out for some fresh air.'

text.content: Moonlight fell upon Su Qingyao's exquisite features, sketching cold contours. She gazed at Chen Ji silently, her eyes deep and unfathomable, as if trying to see through his very soul. This was who knows which time already. Chen Ji's heart警报大作, yet his expression remained unchanged. Su Qingyao was one of the people he feared most in this sect—not because of her strength, but because her intuition was too sharp. Yet tonight, the scrutiny in her eyes seemed lesser, replaced by an inexplicable complexity.

dialogue.content: 'Chen Ji... I have something to say to you.' Su Qingyao suddenly spoke, her voice softer than before, yet more solemn: 'Not as your Senior Sister, nor as the Senior Fellow. Just... Su Qingyao, wanting to exchange a few words with you.' Her gaze fell directly upon Chen Ji, those cold eyes unexpectedly revealing a rare vulnerability. 'May I?'

text.content: Chen Ji was slightly stunned. From the moment he'd known Su Qingyao, this Inner Disciple Senior Fellow had always been cold and resolute, as if nothing in the world could shake her in the slightest. But now, beneath the moonlight, she resembled a hedgehog that had收起所有尖刺, exposing her softest parts to him. He felt wary in his heart, yet knew—some opportunities, once gone, are gone forever. 'Senior Sister, please speak.'

Su Qingyao slowly walked to his side, standing shoulder to shoulder with him. Moonlight flowed like water, pouring over both of them, stretching their shadows long and long. Su Qingyao fell silent for a long while, seemingly considering how to begin. The night wind brushed past, stirring her hair, carrying a faint delicate fragrance. Chen Ji did not rush her, simply waiting quietly. He noticed his heartbeat had quickened from before—not from nervousness, but an inexplicable anticipation.

dialogue.content: 'Do you know about the Saint Candidate?' Su Qingyao finally spoke, her voice very light, yet like a stone dropped into a still lake, stirring层层涟漪. 'Every three years, the three great sects select Saint Candidates from their core disciples. On the surface it's honor and glory, but actually...' She coldly laughed, a flash of contempt flickering in her eyes: 'Actually, they're nothing but sacrificial offerings pushed onto the altar.'

text.content: Chen Ji's pupils slightly contracted. He wasn't completely ignorant of the Saint Candidate matter. While secretly gathering intelligence, he'd heard of this secret existence—every generation of Saint Candidate would ultimately be 'sacrificed' in some ritual, becoming part of the sect's accumulated foundations. He hadn't expected Su Qingyao to be one of them. No wonder she always came and went alone, no wonder her eyes often carried that ageless索沧桑... So she too was a pitiful person caught in fate's grip.

dialogue.content: 'When I was five years old, I was tested and found to have a special constitution.' Su Qingyao's voice was very calm, as if narrating someone else's story. 'The elders of Tianqing Sect were overjoyed, because the spiritual root in my body perfectly matched some ancient ritual. So I was taken in as a core disciple, carefully nurtured, yet no one ever asked if I was willing.' She turned to look at Chen Ji, a hint of self-mockery in her eyes: 'Do you know what's the most ridiculous thing?'

text.content: Chen Ji said nothing, simply quietly awaiting her continuation. Su Qingyao smiled bitterly: 'The most ridiculous thing is, everything I did—desperately cultivating, fighting for the Senior Fellow position—was merely to gain more ability to choose before being sacrificed.' Her voice finally trembled slightly: 'But even if I became Senior Fellow, what then? Their gazes never once regarded me as a person. In their eyes, I was merely a key—a key destined to be used.' Beneath the moonlight, something glistened at the corner of her eye.

dialogue.content: 'Senior Sister Su...' Chen Ji spoke, his voice carrying more warmth than usual. 'So you've been investigating me all this time because of this too?' Su Qingyao was slightly stunned, then gently nodded: 'I always felt you were extraordinary. There's something on you that felt... very familiar to me. That aura of being manipulated by fate yet refusing to submit.' She looked directly into his eyes: 'So I want to know, what's your secret?'

text.content: Moonlight fell silently as Chen Ji sensed the sincerity in Su Qingyao's words. This was the first time he saw Su Qingyao open her heart so completely. She was no longer that aloof Inner Disciple Senior Fellow, merely a woman equally toyed with by fate. Somewhere in his heart, a soft place was gently touched. Perhaps... it was time to take this step.

dialogue.content: 'Senior Sister Su... no, Qingyao.' Chen Ji spoke, his voice low and solemn. This was the first time he called her by name. 'I've actually been waiting for someone. Someone who can understand me.' He raised his head, his gaze meeting Su Qingyao's eyes directly: 'If you're willing to listen, I can tell you my secret—about the Tianji Record, about the future I've seen.' His tone carried an unprecedented seriousness: 'But before that, I need to know—will you trust me?'

text.content: Su Qingyao stared at him in astonishment. Beneath the moonlight, Chen Ji's eyes were no longer that cowardly, mediocre look from daily life, but a depthless tranquility and profoundness. Those eyes seemed to hold seas of stars, making it impossible for her to look away. She suddenly understood something. So this was what she'd been searching for all along—a kindred spirit, standing right before her.

dialogue.content: 'I trust you.' Su Qingyao's voice was light, yet absolutely firm. 'From the first time you lost to me in the Martial Arena yet didn't seem to care at all, I knew you were no ordinary person. For someone who made Han Lie that fool suffer so many times—if you were truly worthless, there'd be no geniuses in this world.' A slight smile curved her lips: 'Go on, I'm listening.'

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath and finally spoke. 'I possess a fragment of the Tianji Record.' His voice was light, yet each word was crystal clear: 'Every time I use it, I can see what will happen within the next three hours. But the price is—each use consumes my precious... Heavenly Fate.' He didn't explain what Heavenly Fate was, but Su Qingyao read the heaviness in his grave tone.

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao's pupils suddenly constricted. Tianji Record—that name was not unfamiliar to her. Legend held it was a supreme treasure left behind by some great being of ancient times, capable of peeking into Heavenly Secrets and foresight. But this treasure had long been lost—no one imagined it would actually be in Chen Ji's hands. 'What have you used this ability for?' Her voice trembled slightly, both from shock and understanding.

text.content: Chen Ji was silent for a moment, then slowly spoke. 'To survive.' Three words, yet heavy as a thousand pounds. 'During these three years at Tianqing Sect, I've used the Tianji Record to avoid countless ambushes and traps. I know who will strike at me and when, which places hold danger, which opportunities can be seized.' He smiled bitterly: 'The so-called waste reputation is merely my best protective color.'

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao gazed at him quietly, her gaze complex. She recalled how Chen Ji had been bullied and humiliated by everyone over these three years, never fighting back. Back then, she'd actually felt something was off—a truly cowardly person, how could they survive in such an environment? So that was how it was. 'You've been pretending this whole time,' she said softly. 'And I... didn't see through it until now.'

text.content: Chen Ji shook his head: 'No, you've already seen clearer than most people.' He turned to look at the moon, his voice carrying a hint of emotion: 'Those truly blinded weren't blind of eye, but blind of heart. They weren't willing to believe a废物 could turn the tables, so even if they saw the truth, they'd choose to look away.' His tone carried a hint of satire: 'The greatest stupidity in this world is self-righteousness.'

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao suddenly burst out laughing. That smile was like ice and snow beginning to thaw, breathtakingly beautiful. 'Chen Ji, you know what? This is the first time I feel your words sound so pleasing to the ear.' She收敛笑意, her gaze softening: 'Since we're both people manipulated by fate, would you... make a pact with me?'

text.content: Chen Ji was slightly stunned: 'What kind of pact?' Su Qingyao took a deep breath, her voice solemn as if taking an oath: 'From now on, no matter what happens, we shall not betray each other.' She paused, then added: 'You are the Tianji Record holder, destined to walk a road bristling with thorns. And I... as a Saint Candidate, also cannot escape the fate of sacrifice. Rather than fighting alone, let's walk together.' Her gaze was sincere and fervent: 'At least on this road, we won't be alone.'

dialogue.content: Chen Ji listened quietly, an indescribable warmth surging in his heart. He thought of Mr. Mo's words, his father's past, his loneliness and concealment all these years. So this was what it felt like to be truly understood. 'Qingyao.' He softly called her name, his voice carrying a warmth never before heard: 'I accept this pact.' He extended his hand, palm upward: 'But I want to add one condition—whichever of us finds a way to break the situation first must pull the other along.'

text.content: Su Qingyao looked at Chen Ji's outstretched hand, a flash of surprise in her eyes that then transformed into relief. Without hesitation, she placed her own hand upon his. Their palms touched, warm sensations passing between them beneath the moonlight. Chen Ji felt the slight trembling in Su Qingyao's fingertips—that was the nervousness of a proud person entrusting her fate to another, and also the anticipation for the future. Moonlight poured down, silvering this moment in a soft glow.

dialogue.content: 'From now on—' Su Qingyao spoke softly, her voice carrying a slight tremor, yet absolutely firm. 'Your fate is my fate.' She clasped Chen Ji's hand, her grip resolute: 'No matter whether the path ahead leads through thorns or abyss, I, Su Qingyao, will never retreat.'

text.content: Chen Ji felt the warmth of her palm, the corners of his mouth slightly rising. This was the first time since arriving in this world that he truly smiled from the heart. 'Alright.' He said softly, his tone carrying a weight of relief: 'Then I also make a vow to you—as long as Chen Ji still has breath in his body, I will never let anyone treat you as a sacrificial offering.' His gaze was profound and earnest: 'The fate of the Saint Candidate, I will rewrite it for you.'

Moonlight was like frost, pouring over both of them. Chen Ji and Su Qingyao's hands were tightly clasped as they made this oath that would change each other's fate on this quiet night. They were no longer merely Senior Sister and junior, but true—companions. The night wind brushed past, bringing a hint of chill, yet unable to disperse the warmth rising between them. Chen Ji suddenly felt perhaps this was what he'd been searching for all along—not the secrets of the Tianji Record, not news of his father, but a partner to walk beside him.

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao suddenly gently tightened her grip on Chen Ji's hand. Hers was very cold, yet gave Chen Ji an inexplicable strength. 'Chen Ji, your hand... is very warm.' She raised her head, her eyes beneath the moonlight clear as water: 'Your fate, I want to rewrite it together with you.'

text.content: These words were like a warm current flowing into Chen Ji's heart. From the moment he'd transmigrated to this world until now, he'd always walked alone in the shadows. Though Mr. Mo's remnant soul offered much guidance, it was merely a wisp of memory; though Ye Qing's alliance had benefits, it carried Demonic Path and transactional undercurrents. Only the person beside him at this moment gave him an unprecedented feeling— He was no longer alone. Chen Ji clasped Su Qingyao's hand in return, a slight smile on his lips: 'Alright.'

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao suddenly laughed softly: 'To think you kept this from me for three years—if it were my past self, I'd definitely have pursued the matter thoroughly.' She released his hand, stepping back, more playfulness appearing in her expression: 'But I'll let it slide tonight. Consider it you paying your dues—by revealing your hand. If you dare deceive me again...' She didn't finish, but the sharpness in her eyes was enough. Chen Ji's lips curved: 'I wouldn't dare.'

text.content: Beneath the moonlight, the two smiled at each other. Chen Ji suddenly realized this was the first time since arriving in this world that he'd truly relaxed. No pretending, no scheming, just simply conversing with another person. This feeling was so unfamiliar it made him somewhat dazed. The night had grown deep; Su Qingyao turned to leave, yet after several steps she looked back. 'Chen Ji, regarding Mr. Mo's matter... whenever you want to talk about it, come find me anytime.' Her voice was gentle: 'Though I may not be able to help much, at least I can listen to you.'

Chen Ji watched her silhouette gradually fade into the moonlight, a complex emotion rising in his heart. Tonight, he'd gained an unexpected ally. No, it should be said... Friend? He silently weighed the word in his heart, a faint smile appearing at the corner of his lips. The night wind gently brushed past; Chen Ji turned to gaze at the night sky. Mr. Mo's secrets still weighed on his heart, but at this moment, his heart was calmer than it had ever been. Because from now on, he was no longer alone.
